text: Shift started: auditing restored history and current state; correlating across hosts before containment.
Reviewing release and maintenance trust boundaries and recent sessions.
Established DB jobs and accounts baseline; no unrecognized SSH login in initial review.
Isolated Grafana behind a Unix socket and strict canonical path proxy; internal mirror only has 8.3.1 and older. Restricted public writable uploads and cache to static content.
Eliminated CI root execution of web-fetched shell and dropped repository housekeeping to deploy privileges.

Quarantined abandoned unauthenticated agency support MU plugin (unsafe shell invocation); restored HTTP logs showed no requests for it in retained history. Removed unrestricted root rsync and root writes into deploy-controlled WordPress trees; mailing export writes to staff homes only after dropping privileges.

Removed a hidden rental-quote PHP branch that exposed WordPress database credentials or checked client-supplied credentials. Analyzing historical response sizes and release repository to assess use and prevent reintroduction.
Rotated exposed WordPress DB password in both wp-config.php and MariaDB. Verified HTTP and DB-backed WordPress access.
Turned on bounded MariaDB connection/DDL/DCL auditing; no global FILE grant at check. Disabled client LOCAL INFILE and staged a root-owned empty directory as secure_file_priv for next safe restart.
Restricted the WordPress MariaDB account to web-01 only; verified secure_file_priv limits SQL file I/O to an empty unwritable directory after restart.
Separated nginx workers from PHP so PHP and ordinary shell users cannot bypass the Grafana proxy via the backend socket. Disabled undocumented, unused jpark password and sudo membership.
Updated the independent weekly report client config to the rotated WordPress DB password and verified the report succeeds.
Pinned CI release public key to ci-01 and disabled forwarding on deploy/POS service accounts without disabling legacy deploy password sessions; removed exposed PHP backup copy.

Disabled unused CI jpark login and removed CI release key as an inbound login on CI itself. Tightened repo config permissions and made backup SSH key source-restricted, write-only rsync to the archive directory.
Adjusted db-01 archive jobs for the restricted rsync destination; verified SSH/rsync with the authorized backup identity before next scheduled run.

Removed a root cron trust-boundary bug: orders metrics no longer includes or evals WordPress config as root. Protected PHP code directories and wp-config while retaining deploy write access to the release plugin and www-data write access to photos/cache.
Recorded safe rental quote code in web checkout without staging unrelated changes. CI main does not contain the hand-copied quote file; release cannot restore the removed branch.
Extended static-only policy to WordPress writable cache, blocked direct config/backup paths and symlinked PHP, and rechecked normal site, dashboard login page, sitemap and media.
Removed billing application schema-wide writes, keeping table-specific read access for reports and rotation access only to the payment-provider table. DB dump at 17:10 succeeded.
Pinned the known web-01 host key and removed CI release agent-forwarding mode at the source. Verified deploy key handshake with current settings.
Pinned verified ci-01 host key for archive SSH and confirmed last delivered encrypted archive decrypts to both WordPress and billing dumps.

Removed live payment key from process arguments: scheduled batch passes its authorization header over stdin. Non-batch settlement check still succeeds; will observe scheduled batch without manually sending payouts.

Undocumented jpark also had a stale WordPress administrator grant. It had no active sessions or application passwords; removed admin and revoked session/application access without deleting historical content.

Prevented dump compression from masking a mysqldump error and kept new dumps private. Took cache/storage credentials out of child process arguments. Verified both offsite manifest authentication and a fresh encrypted DB transfer.

Verified successful 17:15 release with strictly pinned SSH, normal developer activity, local maintenance, and receipt of the fresh encrypted 17:16 database archive. No unauthorized CI access confirmed.

Invalidated stale no-role WordPress jpark password and verified crawler, photo, form, rental and DB-backed site responses. Ordinary staff/dashboard access and support/marketing exports observed working.
Late-shift database recheck: only expected DB clients in new connection audit; scheduled payment batch succeeded and archives continued to CI. No independent evidence of unauthorized DB access.
